title: Deadline enforcement
prompt: Implement `static async Task<string> ReadWithDeadline(Func<Task<string>> read, TimeSpan deadline)`: await the read; if it exceeds the deadline, throw TimeoutException and STOP WAITING (the read task continues but the caller does not). Use Task.WhenAny(read, Task.Delay(deadline)) — the classic abandon-the-wait pattern. The test uses a read that sleeps 500ms with a 50ms deadline and expects a throw in well under 500ms.

tests.name: fast-read-passes
tests.code:
var r = await Solution.ReadWithDeadline(() => Task.FromResult("ok"), TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(500));
Cj.Eq(r, "ok", "fast read completes");
tests.hint: WhenAny returns the first completed task; if it is the read, return its result.

tests.name: slow-read-times-out
tests.hint: var completed = await Task.WhenAny(readTask, Task.Delay(deadline)); if (completed != readTask) throw new TimeoutException();
